source_evidence.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
source_evidence.source_relative_path: Methods/035_HippoRAG Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models.pdf
source_evidence.text:
In contrast, our brains are capable of solving challenging knowledge integration tasks like these with
relative ease. The hippocampal memory indexing theory [75], a well-established theory of human
long-term memory, offers one plausible explanation for this remarkable ability. Teyler and Discenna
[75] propose that our powerful context-based, continually updating memory relies on interactions
between the neocortex, which processes and stores actual memory representations, and the C-shaped
hippocampus, which holds the hippocampal index, a set of interconnected indices which point to
memory units on the neocortex and stores associations between them [19, 76].
In this work, we propose HippoRAG, a RAG framework that serves as a long-term memory for LLMs
by mimicking this model of human memory. Our novel design first models the neocortex’s ability to
process perceptual input by using an LLM to transform a corpus into a schemaless knowledge graph
(KG) as our artificial hippocampal index. Given a new query, HippoRAG identifies the key concepts
in the query and runs the Personalized PageRank (PPR) algorithm [30] on the KG, using the query
concepts as the seeds, to integrate information across passages for retrieval. PPR enables HippoRAG
to explore KG paths and identify relevant subgraphs, essentially performing multi-hop reasoning in a
single retrieval step.

relation_review.evidence: 核对全部必要事实、引用与原文；没有来源时不得补造。
relation_review.semantics: 核对关系方向、实体角色、任务/实验条件和题干前提。
relation_review.uncertainty: 必要证据不足时明确说明缺口；反例允许纠正前提。

scoring_rules.primary: SupportRecall@5; within one fact unit supporting sources are OR, required fact units are AND.
scoring_rules.answer_review: Per-case atomic reference criteria, scored 0/1 each by a named reviewer; evidence support and citation location checked separately.
scoring_rules.graph_coverage: Source-backed expected subgraphs are a reference check, not measured retrieval success or answer correctness.
scoring_rules.denominator: 32 answerable questions; 24 cross-paper relation questions reported separately; 8 negative cases reported separately.
scoring_rules.interpretation: retrieval coverage, citation validity, graph-path coverage and semantic answer correctness are separate results; no assumption that graph wins.
scoring_rules.semantic_score: Number of supported satisfied atomic criteria / all criteria. This is not calculated by source ID recall.
scoring_rules.semantic_pass: All criteria satisfied with supporting citations; no critical unsupported claim. Negatives must correct/reject the premise within the evidence boundary.
critical_errors: 伪造继承/评测/全称优越性
混淆预算耗尽与正确答案
scoring_rules.reporting: Overview, per-category metrics, charts, latency, tokens and full paired details must coexist after real execution.
